title: Complex Multi-Row Arrangements
tagline: Year 4 — Three rows of three: front, behind, left, right and diagonal clues on a grid

introduction.overview: A multi-row arrangement places people in a grid of rows and columns instead of a single line. Each person has two coordinates, so clues are of four kinds: row clues (same row, front row), column clues (same column, directly behind), neighbour clues in a row (immediate left or right) and diagonal clues. The method is to draw the grid, write coordinates for each placed person, and let each clue fix one coordinate.
introduction.placementRelevance: Grid arrangements appear as the harder variant of seating puzzles in company tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Seat plans, warehouse shelves and classroom layouts are grids.

learningObjectives: Draw and label a grid with coordinates
Interpret front, behind, left, right and diagonal clues
Use corner and centre clues as anchors

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Facing north, left is west. "Behind" means the next row back in the same column.

coreDefinitions: Grid: rows and columns of seats.
Directly behind: next row, same column.
Anchor: a corner or centre clue that fixes a seat exactly.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A grid puzzle is two line puzzles at once; every clue fixes a row, a column, or both.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw a 3 × 3 box, mark anchors first, then use behind and left clues to extend, and finally use same-row or same-column clues.

mainNarrative: Nine friends sit in 3 rows. A is in the front row at the east end; F is immediately left of A, so F is front row centre. D is directly behind A (middle row east end) and G is directly behind D (back row east end).
B is in the centre. H is immediately left of B, so H is middle row west. I is directly behind B (back row centre). E is back row west.
The front row west is left for C. The grid is C F A / H B D / E I G.
Same-row and same-column clues are weaker; use them to choose between two remaining seats.
Always read the finished grid against each clue.

deepDiveAspects.title: Anchors
deepDiveAspects.content: Corner and centre clues give exact coordinates; start there.

deepDiveAspects.title: Direction conventions
deepDiveAspects.content: Check the facing direction: left and right swap if the group faces south.

solvedExamples.title: Anchor and chain
solvedExamples.question: A is front row east end; D is directly behind A; G is directly behind D. Where is G?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Move one row back each time.

solvedExamples.title: Left clue
solvedExamples.question: B is at the centre and H is immediately left of B. Where is H?

solvedExamples.title: Grid
solvedExamples.question: The grid is C F A / H B D / E I G (front to back). Who sits directly behind B?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: I is in the back row.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Draw a 3 × 3 box, mark anchors, extend with behind and left clues, use group clues last.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A person cannot occupy two seats.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Weak clues decide only at the end.

easy.question:
Nine friends A to I sit in three rows of three seats, all facing north. The front row is the northernmost row. Left means west. The following facts are known:
1. A sits in the front row at the east end.
2. F sits immediately to the left of A.
3. B sits in the middle row at the centre.
4. D sits directly behind A.
5. H sits immediately to the left of B.
6. G sits directly behind D.
7. I sits directly behind B.
8. E sits in the back row at the west end.

Who sits in the front row at the east end?
easy.explanation: The rows (front to back) are C F A / H B D / E I G, so A sits there.
